clue.text: Hold animal with tight grip

explanation.surface: A handler restrains a creature by gripping it tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling clasp around the body is a kind of hold, named after the way a large mammal crushes its prey.

clue.text: Plagues of animals

explanation.walkthrough: Plagues looks like a noun, as in plagues of locusts, but it is the verb for nagging.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to harass them repeatedly, and the same word names the striped nocturnal burrowing creatures.

clue.text: In favour of taking a very quiet wander

definitions.note: the answer is a verb, 'to be in favour of'

parts.note: pianissimo, the musical mark for very soft

explanation.surface: Someone supports going for a silent stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve of something is to support it or think well of it, which is being in favour of it.

clue.text: Greeting male students with love

parts.note: two learners, L being a learner driver's plate
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A man warmly welcomes his students with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the commonest word said when meeting someone, so it is a salutation.

clue.text: Somehow get marine to develop

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged any way that works

explanation.surface: Someone must find a way to turn a recruit into a proper marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds germinate when they sprout and begin to grow, an intransitive sense of develop.

clue.text: Seems to be a quiet pair, reportedly coming to the point

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: the fruit sounds the same as a couple
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A quiet couple apparently get down to business at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe giving an outward impression or looking a certain way to an observer.

clue.text: Get your gun, girl!

definitions.note: a title fragment: the name it completes is the answer
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the name that opens the title of Irving Berlin's musical about a sharpshooter

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an order to arm yourself, but the words finish the title of the musical Annie Get Your Gun, about the markswoman Annie Oakley.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Wild West musical is a girl, and her name is a common female first name.

clue.text: Frightened of becoming frozen?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: turned to stone, rigid

explanation.walkthrough: Fear makes a person freeze on the spot, so both senses meet in a body rigid with terror.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both terrified and literally turned to stone, set hard and immobile.

clue.text: A doctor that is not contracted in the area

parts.note: Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree
id est, Latin for that is
the shortened form of not, as in don't

explanation.surface: A local doctor who has not been signed up for a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the surrounding environment, such as the conditions or sound present all around.

clue.text: Good person's misplaced pity about to become stauncher

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong spots, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint's mercy is directed wrongly and turns into firmer loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Stauncher looks like a comparative adjective, more loyal, but it is a noun: something that staunches, or stops, bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic is a substance that stops bleeding when applied to a cut, so it staunches the flow.

clue.text: Pop led with right cunningly, having this kind of effect

indicators.note: doing something cunningly means twisting it craftily, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pop group's leader teams up with someone else, slyly creating an effect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doppler effect is the change in pitch of a sound as its source moves past, like a passing siren.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's name is attached to the familiar shift in observed frequency, so it names that kind of effect.

clue.text: In a significant way, but without skill!

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: not done competently

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT ABLY and it means clumsily, the opposite of the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means especially or in a remarkable manner, as in a point worth mentioning above others.

clue.text: Cut back for English firm in some confusion

indicators.note: confusion jumbles things, so the preceding pair of short words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled English company is forced to trim its spending.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to reduce spending or consumption, which is what cutting back on expenses means.

clue.text: Still at home with the Queen last night

parts.note: being in means being at home
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

explanation.surface: Someone spent a quiet night in, entertaining royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert is motionless and inactive, which is the adjectival sense of still.

clue.text: Takes turns to have beef

indicators.note: taking turns suggests letters changing places, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: People take it in turns to eat some beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick slice of beef cut for grilling or frying is the commonest example of this cut of meat.

clue.text: Collapses suddenly after sleek turn

indicators.note: to turn something is to twist it around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: over can mean finished, done with, as after can

explanation.surface: Someone faints straight after a smooth pirouette.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards here: the rearranged word comes first, followed by the word meaning after or past.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to fall down abruptly, like a capsizing boat, so it means toppling without warning.

clue.text: Not believing ices that I consumed

indicators.note: food that is consumed is broken down, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to having eaten the ice creams, with a sceptical aside.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheistic outlook rejects belief in any god, so it describes someone without religious faith.

clue.text: Sweetheart's hunt for insects' nest

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A lover is on the lookout for a bees' nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The waxy hexagonal cells built by bees to hold their honey and young form their home.

clue.text: Clean home prepared for reptile

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready by working it over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy house is made ready for a pet lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: This colour-changing lizard is a specific example of the cold-blooded scaly animals.

clue.text: Order for business with 2,000 included

indicators.note: something included is placed inside, so the thousands go into the middle

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, twice

explanation.surface: A firm puts in an order for two thousand units.
explanation.definitionFit: A command is an instruction given with authority, the noun sense of an order.

clue.text: Parts of speech about brave Detective Sergeant

indicators.note: turned about means moved around, so the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: standard abbreviation of the police rank

explanation.surface: Speeches praising a courageous police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverbs are one of the grammatical word classes, modifying verbs and adjectives, so they are parts of speech.

clue.text: Dickens' artful one has no right to cheat

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the name

parts.note: the Artful Dodger is the pickpocket in Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: The Artful Dodger, a born rogue, has no right to swindle anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the R from the character's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge can mean to evade by trickery, so it serves as a verb for swindling or cheating.

clue.text: Damned American pet has disappeared!

explanation.surface: An American complains that the blasted pet has run off.
explanation.walkthrough: American flags the word as US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggone is a mild US euphemism for goddamn, used as a milder curse word.

clue.text: Antiquated "C" in text rewritten

indicators.note: rewriting text produces a fresh version, so the letters are set down in a new order

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned letter C in a document gets revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extinct has died out completely, a stronger form of being outdated or obsolete.

clue.text: Ladybird?

parts.note: surface reading: the small spotted beetle
setter's reading: split in two, a woman's name that is also the name of a bird

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the word is not the beetle: read it as lady plus bird, a name shared by a woman and an old word for the song thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis is both a female given name and a poetic or dialect word for the song thrush.

clue.text: With lusty outsiders, we fight devious boxer

indicators.note: a devious route twists about, so the letters wander into a new order
outsiders are on the edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of lusty

explanation.surface: Pugnacious types boast of fighting dirty against a prizefighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in the lightest professional weight class, so the word names a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Declines passing fancies without a point

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece stands around the other

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Trends that pass and lack any purpose eventually decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade is to grow weaker or dwindle, the intransitive sense of declining.

clue.text: Exceptionally wide, for example

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket, a run conceded without the batter scoring

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, gives a free run called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb it means more than usually, and in cricket it names a bonus run such as a wide.

clue.text: Dive badly after a bishop appeared

indicators.note: a dive done badly goes wrong, so its letters fall out of order

parts.note: Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A clumsy plunge into the pool after a churchman showed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To have arrived is to have turned up or come into view, the same as having appeared.

clue.text: In the Open, used to be exhausted

parts.note: clothes that have been used are worn

explanation.surface: Something left out in the open used to be tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: Outworn means used up or worn out through age and use, so it describes something spent.

clue.text: Wants of French fathers

parts.note: sires are male parents, especially of animals

explanation.surface: A wish list belonging to French dads.
explanation.definitionFit: As nouns, wants and desires are both longings or things a person wishes to have.

clue.text: Most macho of two items of underwear

parts.note: second item: in Britain, a vest is a sleeveless undershirt

explanation.surface: Wearing a bra and vest hardly seems the most manly look.
explanation.walkthrough: The two garments are a bra and, in British usage, a vest, the sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The bravest person shows the greatest courage, the quality a tough macho image claims most of.
